title: White Noise: private chats on Nostr
summary: Razor shows how end-to-end encrypted chat really works, from mixing a shared key to catching a man in the middle. Then we point White Noise at our own Nostr relay and look at what a relay can actually see.
share_text: Can your chats be switched off? Notes (and 5 mini-games) from the @CodeOrangeDevs workshop on White Noise and private messaging on Nostr
tldr: Every chat app needs something in the middle to hold your messages while you are offline. The question is who runs it and what it can read.
Encrypting is the easy part. The hard part is two people agreeing on a key over a line anyone can watch, and knowing the key really belongs to your friend.
White Noise keeps the encryption (MLS) and swaps the company server for Nostr relays that anyone can run, so there is no single off switch.
Old-style Nostr DMs hide the text but show who messaged whom and when. Gift wrap is the fix, and it is still being finished.

resources.note: the messaging app we tested: end-to-end encrypted chats and groups that travel over Nostr relays instead of one company's servers

resources.title: BitChat
resources.note: chat over Bluetooth with people nearby, no internet needed. It can also show an ecash token as a tidy card instead of a long string

resources.title: Keychat
resources.note: another Nostr chat app that mixes messaging and ecash. Mentioned at the end, saved for a later session

resources.title: Signal: what is a safety number?
resources.note: the number (or QR code) you compare with a friend to check nobody is sitting in the middle of your chat

resources.title: Messaging Layer Security (MLS), RFC 9420
resources.note: the open standard White Noise uses to agree on keys, including in group chats

resources.title: Marmot protocol
resources.note: the glue between MLS and Nostr: how keys and group messages are stored and passed around on relays

resources.title: NIP-59: Gift wrap
resources.note: wraps a message so relays can't tell who sent it or exactly when. The kind 1059 events we saw on the relay

resources.title: NIP-44: Encrypted payloads
resources.note: the encryption used inside the gift wrap

resources.title: Noise Protocol Framework
resources.note: the key exchange building blocks BitChat uses, built on Diffie-Hellman

resources.title: strfry
resources.note: the Nostr relay software Razor ran for the experiment. It supports small plugins, which he used to log every event that arrived

resources.title: Blossom
resources.note: simple media servers for Nostr. Photos and files go here, short messages go to relays

resources.title: Primal
resources.note: Nostr client used for the demo: log in read-only with anyone's public key and see who sent them old-style DMs

resources.title: Computerphile
resources.note: Razor's pick for going deeper: look for their videos on Diffie-Hellman, end-to-end encryption, the Signal protocol and group messaging

resources.title: Cashu
resources.note: ecash for Bitcoin. A token is just a string of text, so any chat app can carry it
